chunks: We have made you a temperate people that you act as witness over man, and the Prophet as witness over you. We decreed the Qiblah which you faced before that We may know who follow the Apostle and who turn away in haste. And this was a hard (test) except for those who were guided by God. But God will not suffer your faith to go waste, for God is to men full of mercy and grace.

key_terms.يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ: turns away in haste / turns back on his heels

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the change of Qiblah in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'wasat' (middle) is interpreted not merely as moderation but as a unique status of justice and balance, positioning the Ummah as impartial witnesses to humanity's deeds. The shift of the Qiblah is viewed as a divine trial to distinguish true adherence to the Prophet from mere ritualistic continuity, emphasizing that the previous prayers offered toward Jerusalem remain valid and accepted by God. This verse underscores the concept of 'Iman' (faith) as an enduring spiritual capital that God preserves, reflecting His mercy even during periods of transitional testing.
